name: Bristol
description: Bristol is a patience (solitaire) card game played with a single standard 52-card deck. It is a fan-type layout in the style of La Belle Lucie, with building regardless of suit on both the foundations and the tableau, and is considered relatively easy to win.

content.text: Bristol is a patience (solitaire) card game played with a single standard 52-card deck. It is a fan-type layout in the style of La Belle Lucie, with building regardless of suit on both the foundations and the tableau, and is considered relatively easy to win.

Country/Region of Origin: United States
Time Period: Around 1950
Historical Development: Invented by the card game authors Morehead and Mott-Smith as a fan-type patience closely related to La Belle Lucie.
Cultural Significance: Known as an easy-to-win solitaire, included in classic card game collections.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Cards per Player: Varies by player count
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise

items.text: Belvedere: Belvedere is a closely related patience in which an ace is removed from the deck before the deal and immediately set up as a foundation, but play otherwise follows the normal rules of Bristol.
House rules and table variants: Players sometimes adjust small details such as redeal limits or whether gaps in the tableau may be filled, but core Bristol structure and building rules stay the same.
